Live re-derived local-only in-scope count: 9 blanket suppressions across 9 actionable files remain (down from 32/25 at cycle 24 close), plus 5 permanent exceptions (4 pre-existing + Elimination.lean new this cycle) and the deliberately-deferred 6-suppression count-6 file. Re-baselined the check-lint-suppressions.sh ratchet after every reduction (final state: 46 -> 34 blanket suppressions repo-wide -- 20 local-only in-scope + 14 upstream-shared, unchanged). Plan fully updated (commit b0d493af): RESUME HERE section rewritten with cycle-25 per-file results, a live re-derived count-1 tier survey (9 actionable + 5 permanent exceptions), two new findings (P5 dangling-by parse hazard; C7 linter.privateModule category), and cold-start instructions; plan header, Phase 5 heading stats, and the Definition-of-Done suppression-audit criterion all updated to 331/103/9; a Phase-5-body 'Done (cycle 25)' backfill table added with commit hashes. Full CSLib CI pipeline re-run at cycle end and confirmed green: lake build --wfail --iofail exactly 5 baseline sorry warnings (zero new), checkInitImports clean, lake lint zero matches on the 7 prevention categories, lake shake exactly the 12 upstream-shared files (zero local-only), lake exe mk_all --check no update necessary, lake test exit 0, check-lint-suppressions.sh exit 0 (34, baseline ceiling 34). git diff on every commit individually confirmed zero sorry lines touched and no proof term/definition/theorem statement altered; every downstream importer of every edited file was rebuilt green before that file's commit. Neither Phase 7 blocker was re-investigated (both CLOSED by prior user decision) and neither is carried forward as open in this handoff. Task remains PARTIAL pending a fresh /implement or /orchestrate dispatch to continue Phase 5.
decisions_made: Started with WitnessSeed.lean per the continuation handoff's explicit NEXT TARGET, then continued into DenseValidity.lean to close the count-2 tier entirely before moving into the count-1 tier, smallest-first.

For WitnessSeed.lean's 36 emptyLine sites, verified every flagged line was a genuinely bare blank line (no content) before batch-deleting them in descending line-number order -- whitespace-only, no elaboration change, confirmed via full scoped rebuild plus all 4 direct downstream importers.

Used a generic Python word-wrap script for longLine fixes (split at the last space before column 100, continuation indented +4), which worked cleanly for the large majority of sites but broke Bridge.lean's futureMono signature by leaving `by` dangling alone on its own line -- diagnosed via the resulting checkColGt/unsolved-goals errors and fixed by hand-wrapping the type signature instead. Recorded as new finding P5; will apply the same caution to any remaining def-signature-ending-in-by sites in future cycles.

For Elimination.lean's linter.privateModule suppression, did not simply trust the file's existing rationale comment -- removed the suppression and rebuilt to directly verify the warning reappears at 1:0 regardless of the already-present @[expose] public section, then restored the suppression with the verification recorded inline. Classified as a new permanent exception (C7 category) rather than force-narrowing a module-wide diagnostic that has no declaration-level attachment point.

For TemporalContent.lean, removed both the suppression and its adjacent comment claiming the suppression was structurally required for blank lines between declarations inside @[expose] public section -- that specific claim was falsified by the zero-warnings-on-removal result, so the incorrect comment was not preserved.

Re-baselined check-lint-suppressions.sh after every single file's commit (not batched to cycle end), matching the Method section's 'in the same commit as the file' instruction more precisely than prior cycles.

Ran the full CSLib CI pipeline (all 8 steps except the cache fetch, which was already warm) once at cycle end rather than after every file, since per-file scoped rebuilds plus downstream-importer rebuilds already provided per-commit verification granularity matching Phase 5's Tier-4 rule.

Fully rewrote the plan's RESUME HERE section rather than appending, consistent with prior cycles' established practice. Also updated the plan header effort estimate, Phase 5 heading stats, Baseline-and-current-state table's suppression row, and the Definition-of-Done suppression-audit criterion.

Stopped after 11 files (46 -> 34 suppressions) to close out cleanly with the full CI pipeline, ratchet re-baseline, plan rewrite, and handoff, rather than start a larger count-1-tier file (Defs.lean 655 lines or Tableau.lean 1208 lines) and risk an incomplete state at cycle end.
Did not attempt Interface.lean (3048 lines, count-6 tier, deliberately deferred) or re-investigate either of Phase 7's closed blockers, matching this task's standing scope constraints.
dead_ends: The generic word-wrap Python script is unsafe to apply blindly to any line ending in `:= by` or containing a trailing `at <hyp>` clause -- both can produce a dangling continuation token that breaks tactic-block parsing even though the wrap is otherwise 'safe' whitespace-only surgery everywhere else. Future cycles should grep the target-line list for lines ending in `by` or `at` before running the generic wrapper, and hand-wrap those specifically.

IMPORTANT new hazard: P5 in Accumulated findings -- when wrapping a `def X ... := by` signature that exceeds the 100-char line limit, never let `by` dangle alone on its own continuation line (breaks the tactic block's column reference, producing 'expected * or checkColGt' plus a cascading 'unsolved goals' on the NEXT declaration, easy to misattribute). Fix: wrap the type signature instead, keep ':= by' attached to line end. Same principle for `simp only [...] at h` -- wrap inside the bracket list, not after `at`. If reusing a generic word-wrap script, pre-filter target lines for a trailing `by` or `at` token and hand-wrap those specifically.
